How can you sell a house in Milwaukee when time matters?

Most Milwaukee owners choose between three routes: list with an agent, sell the house yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the property as it stands. The route that fits depends on the condition of the house, any open city orders, and how soon you need the money.

The Census Bureau estimated Milwaukee's population at 562,407 on July 1, 2025, down 2.7 percent from the April 2020 estimates base. Only 41.8 percent of housing units are owner-occupied, so a large share of Milwaukee houses that change hands are rentals, duplexes and investor-owned property. The median value of an owner-occupied home was $184,000 for 2020 to 2024.

What kind of housing and neighborhoods does Milwaukee have?

Milwaukee sits on the western shore of Lake Michigan where the Milwaukee, Menomonee and Kinnickinnic rivers meet, and it is the seat of Milwaukee County. It was incorporated in 1846 and covers roughly 96 square miles of land, with about 6,001 people per square mile in 2020.

The housing stock reflects that history. The city is nicknamed Cream City for the pale local brick used on many older buildings, and its residential blocks include many Polish flats, two-family homes with one unit stacked above the other. An owner who lives upstairs and rents downstairs, or an heir who inherits a flat, often sells with tenants in place, so the lease terms matter to any buyer.

  • Revitalized areas named in the city's history include the Historic Third Ward, Lincoln Village, the East Side, Walker's Point and Bay View.
  • Bronzeville grew out of the Great Migration, and the South Side around Mitchell Street and Lincoln Village is tied to the city's Polish community.
  • Walker's Point takes its name from developer George H. Walker, who built a log house there in 1834.

What do schools, roads and jobs add to a Milwaukee listing?

Milwaukee Public Schools serves almost all of the city. It is the largest district in Wisconsin, with 69,115 students in 2021-2022 and 156 schools, and the city also has more than two dozen private or parochial high schools. Buyers with children will ask which attendance area or school option applies, so be ready to point them to the district.

Interstates 43 and 94 meet at the Marquette Interchange downtown, and Interstate 794 runs along the lakefront toward Bay View. Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport sits on the southern edge of the city, and The Hop streetcar links the Intermodal Station, downtown and the Lower East Side. Five Fortune 500 companies have headquarters here, and health care makes up about 27 percent of city jobs.

Weather is part of the sale too. Milwaukee averages about 48.7 inches of snow a year and 34.57 inches of precipitation, so buyers' inspectors look closely at roofs, gutters and basements.

What does the City of Milwaukee require when a house is sold?

The Department of Neighborhood Services (DNS) runs the main local checks. Its Title Search page strongly urges a DNS title search on every Milwaukee real estate transaction, because the form shows pending code violations, special charges and city programs that govern the property. The page states that the new owner is responsible for any unabated code violations.

  • Property registration: non-owner-occupied residential property and commercial property must be registered with DNS. Owner-occupied one-family, two-family and condo units are generally exempt. A seller uses the Seller Notification Form (DNS-8D) to tell DNS that ownership changed. Call (414) 286-8569 with questions.
  • Vacant building registration: a building left vacant for 30 days or more must be registered. A buyer of a vacant building registers within 30 days, and the seller must tell the buyer in plain terms that the registration is required. Listing the building for sale does not remove the duty.
  • Estates: a vacant property in probate is exempt when the personal representative or executor lives within the seven-county area around Milwaukee.
  • Open orders: DNS posts violations in its Land Management System, and you can call the section that issued an order.

The vacant building rules are in the city's Vacant Building FAQs. There is no fee for the first six months of registration, and renewals after that carry fees that DNS lists.

Which Wisconsin rules apply to a Milwaukee sale?

Sellers of one-to-four unit homes must complete a real estate condition report under Wis. Stat. 709.02. The buyer must receive it within 10 days after the seller accepts the contract, and a buyer who does not may rescind within two business days after those 10 days end. A court-appointed fiduciary who never lived in the house is excused, which matters for estate sales.

Under Wis. Stat. 77.22 the grantor pays a transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value. On a $200,000 sale that works out to $600. Transfers by will, or between a parent and child for nominal consideration, are among the exemptions listed in section 77.25. The return is filed electronically with the Department of Revenue, and the register of deeds collects the fee at recording.

How do you record the deed in Milwaukee County?

The Milwaukee County Register of Deeds is at 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103. Recording costs $30 per document no matter the page count, plus the transfer fee shown on your e-RETR receipt. The office takes cash, check or money order, and it does not take credit or debit cards.

  1. Prepare the deed with an attorney or title company, because the register cannot draft or review documents.
  2. File the electronic transfer return with the Department of Revenue and print the receipt.
  3. Submit the original deed, receipt and payment in person or by mail.

Documents are recorded in order of receipt within three to five business days, and the original is mailed back within one to two weeks. Questions go to (414) 278-4005.

How do assessments and tax bills affect a Milwaukee seller?

The Milwaukee Assessor's Office typically revalues the whole city every year and did so for 2026. Open Book for 2026 ran from April 20 to May 18, 2026, and that window has closed, so check the assessor's page for the next schedule. You can look up any property's assessed value at assessments.milwaukee.gov, and the assessor's phone line is (414) 286-6565.

The Department of Revenue's Guide for Property Owners explains that assessments reflect market value as of January 1. Clerks mail bills by the third Monday in December. If you pay in installments, the first is due January 31 and the second July 31, and an unpaid first installment becomes fully delinquent on February 1 with interest at 1 percent a month. Ask your title company how the current year's tax will be divided between you and the buyer at closing.

What if the Milwaukee house is a short-term rental or has tenants?

DNS administers the state tourist rooming house license for stays shorter than one month, and an owner who is ending that use submits a surrender form. Tenants and registration status are the usual issues in a rental sale, so gather leases, rent rolls and DNS registration records before you speak with buyers.

A cash buyer can purchase a tenant-occupied duplex or a house with open orders as it stands. Whichever route you take, ask for the offer in writing and compare the net amount after your mortgage payoff, city charges and closing costs.

More questions about Milwaukee, WI

Does Milwaukee require a title search before I sell?

The city strongly urges one on every transaction but its page does not call it a legal requirement. The DNS title search shows open violations, special charges and registration duties, so it protects both sides.

Who pays the Wisconsin real estate transfer fee?

The seller, who is the grantor, pays it under Wis. Stat. 77.22 at 30 cents per $100 of value. The register of deeds collects it when the deed is recorded, and exempt transfers such as those by will owe nothing.

Do I have to register a vacant Milwaukee house I am selling?

Yes, if the building has been vacant 30 days or more and no exemption applies. Listing it for sale does not excuse the duty, and the buyer must register within 30 days of buying.

How long does recording a deed take in Milwaukee County?

The register records documents within three to five business days, in the order received. Paper originals come back by mail within one to two weeks.

Must I give the buyer a condition report?

Yes for most one-to-four unit homes. The report is due within 10 days after the contract is accepted, and a fiduciary who never occupied the home is exempt under Wis. Stat. 709.01.

How can you sell a house fast in Madison, WI?

A Madison owner can list with an agent, sell privately, or take an as-is cash offer, and the paperwork after the contract looks the same for all three. The state transfer return, the seller's condition report and the recorded deed apply whichever route you choose. Speed mostly depends on how little the house needs before a buyer can close.

Madison has a large rental base, and that shapes who sells here. The Census Bureau puts the owner-occupied rate at 46.0% for 2020 to 2024, so many sellers are landlords or heirs holding a unit that is leased or empty. Tenants, an unfinished permit or a short-term rental permit each add steps that a plain owner-occupied sale skips.

What should a seller know about Madison itself?

Madison is the state capital, in the middle of Dane County, 77 miles west of Milwaukee and 122 miles northwest of Chicago. Downtown sits on an isthmus between Lake Mendota and Lake Monona, and the city wraps around the separate municipalities of Maple Bluff, Monona and Shorewood Hills. It also borders Sun Prairie, Middleton, McFarland and Fitchburg. On October 31, 2022, Madison annexed most of the remaining Town of Madison, so confirm the municipality printed on your tax bill before assuming which rules apply.

More than 120 neighborhood associations are officially recognized. The Marquette neighborhood on the near east side includes the Marquette Bungalows Historic District and the Orton Park Historic District, and Dudgeon-Monroe near Lake Wingra and the Hilldale area are other named areas buyers search by. Ask the city whether a historic district covers your block.

Jobs come from the state government, UW-Madison (more than 25,000 faculty and staff), UW Health, Meriter, St. Mary's, and employers such as Exact Sciences and Promega. The Madison Metropolitan School District serves the city with about 25,000 students in 46 schools, including Vel Phillips Memorial, Madison West, Madison East and La Follette high schools. US 12, known locally as the Beltline, serves the south and west sides, while I-39, I-90 and I-94 run along the far east edge.

What do the Census numbers say about Madison homes?

The figures below describe Madison as a whole, and your own street may sit well above or below them. They help you judge whether an offer is in the right range before you ask for comparable sales.

What if the Madison house has been a short-term rental?

The permit does not pass to the buyer. Madison issues a ZTRHP permit to a specific host for a specific dwelling unit, and the permit is not transferable. The city calls these rentals short-term when guests stay fewer than 30 nights, and Wisconsin law calls them tourist rooming houses. If you advertised the house on Airbnb or VRBO, close out the listings and tell the buyer the permit ends with you.

These are the rules the city lists for permit holders:

  • The unit must be the host's primary dwelling while the rental runs and for the 12 consecutive months before it began.
  • When the host is away, the rental may operate no more than 30 days per licensing year, which runs July 1 to June 30.
  • Maximum guests are the lesser of twice the number of legal bedrooms or 12 people, and children under 12 do not count.
  • The permit costs a $300 one-time application fee and $100 a year to renew.
  • Violations carry fines of $500 to $1,000 per day, and the city can revoke the permit.

A Transient Room Tax permit from the city Finance Department and a license from Public Health Madison and Dane County are also required, and the city will not issue the ZTRHP permit until both are in hand. Ask Building Inspection to confirm your permit status in writing before you list the house.

How do rentals and tenants affect a Madison sale?

Tenants stay in place while you sell, so the buyer inherits the lease and the maintenance history. Madison Building Inspection takes complaints from tenants when a housing provider is slow to repair problems, and a complaint on file can surface in a buyer's questions. Fix open items first and keep repair receipts together.

Check the lease for its end date and any notice terms before you promise a closing date. If you want the unit vacant at closing, plan the timeline around the lease and the state landlord-tenant rules published by the Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection, which the city links as a resource for owners.

How does the Madison assessment calendar work?

The assessor values property as of January 1, and the objection steps run in spring and summer. For 2026, notices were mailed May 1, the Open Book window ran May 4 to 8, and objections to the Board of Assessors were due by 4:30 p.m. on May 15. Those 2026 dates have passed, so a 2027 appeal would follow the dates the Assessor's Office posts next spring.

Open Book is for correcting facts such as room counts or a permit that was not finished by January 1. If the facts are right but the value is not, you file an objection with the Board of Assessors, and the Board of Review is the final municipal step. Call 608-266-4531 or email openbook@cityofmadison.com. Commercial and multi-unit owners must include income and expense information with an objection.

What does Wisconsin require from a Madison seller?

Two state rules apply to almost every sale. The seller pays a transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value, set by Wis. Stat. 77.22, and the seller of a one-to-four unit property must furnish a condition report under Wis. Stat. 709.02. At the Madison median home value of $372,900, the fee works out to about $1,119.

  • The condition report is due within 10 days after the contract is accepted. A buyer who does not receive it can rescind within 2 business days after that 10-day period.
  • Court-appointed fiduciaries who never lived in the property are excused from the report.
  • Transfers by will or descent, foreclosure deeds to the lender and transfers between spouses are among the fee exemptions listed by the Department of Revenue.
  • A false or understated value on the return can bring a penalty of $25 or 25% of the extra fee, whichever is greater.

A cash buyer purchasing as-is still receives the report, and the return is still filed.

How is the deed recorded in Dane County?

The Dane County Register of Deeds records the deed for a $30 fee per document, and an Electronic Transfer Return receipt must accompany it. The deed must name the grantor and grantee, carry the grantor's notarized signature, include the legal description and the parcel number from the tax bill, and list a return address. Only the original deed with original signatures can be recorded, not a photocopy.

You can mail the package to the Dane County Register of Deeds, PO Box 1438, Madison, WI 53701-1438, with the recording fee and any transfer fee combined on one check. The office takes questions at (608) 266-4141. Deeds are usually drafted by an attorney or title company, and the office cannot fill them out for you.

More questions about Madison, WI

Do I need a permit to rent my Madison house short term?

Yes. Madison requires a ZTRHP permit before you advertise or rent, and the house must be your primary dwelling. You also need a Transient Room Tax permit and a Public Health license. The city charges a $300 application fee and $100 a year to renew.

Does a short-term rental permit transfer to the buyer of my Madison house?

No. The city issues the permit to a specific host for a specific unit, and it cannot be transferred. A buyer who wants to operate a short-term rental must apply on their own and meet the primary-dwelling rule.

Who pays the Wisconsin transfer fee when I sell in Madison?

The seller pays it. Wis. Stat. 77.22 sets the fee at 30 cents per $100 of value, collected when the deed is recorded. Some transfers, such as those by will or between spouses, are exempt.

How long does the Madison buyer have to receive the condition report?

Ten days after the contract is accepted. If the report does not arrive in that time, the buyer has 2 business days after the 10-day period ends to rescind and recover deposits under Wis. Stat. 709.02.

Where do I record a deed for a Madison house?

File it with the Dane County Register of Deeds. The recording fee is $30 per document, and you must include the Electronic Transfer Return receipt. The mailing address is PO Box 1438, Madison, WI 53701-1438.

How can I sell a house fast in Green Bay?

You can list the house, sell it on your own, or take a cash offer, and the cash route is the quickest because the buyer does not wait on a lender. Which option fits depends on the condition of the house, who lives in it, and how much time you have before a payment or a move comes due.

  • Listing: the usual route for a house that shows well. It brings the widest pool of buyers and the longest timeline.
  • Selling by owner: you keep control of price and showings and do the contract and disclosure work yourself.
  • Cash offer: built for inherited houses, rentals with tenants, houses with code or repair problems, and sellers facing a deadline.

Green Bay is a city of about 106,675 people, so houses range from older homes near the river to newer blocks farther out. A buyer who pays cash will price the house on its condition and location, so gather repair estimates and permit records before you talk numbers.

What should a seller know about Green Bay itself?

Green Bay is the county seat of Brown County and sits at the mouth of the Fox River on the bay of Lake Michigan, about 90 miles north of Milwaukee. Wikipedia notes that Interstate 43 meets Interstate 41 here. The city covers 55.76 square miles, of which 45.48 are land, and about 14 percent of it lies inside the Oneida Nation reservation.

Jean Nicolet is believed to have landed near the site in 1634, and a French fur-trading post followed. Charles Michel de Langlade, who is generally credited as the first permanent European settler in Wisconsin, settled in Green Bay in the 1760s. The Tank Cottage, built in 1776, is the oldest standing building from the state's early years and now sits at Heritage Hill State Historical Park in neighboring Allouez.

That long history shows up in the housing stock. Winters are the main wear on a house: the January mean temperature is 16.6 degrees, and 68 days a year stay at or below freezing. Roofs, furnaces and basements take the brunt of that cold, so keep receipts for any recent work on them to show a buyer.

Which Green Bay projects need a permit, and what if I skipped one?

Green Bay requires a building permit for most projects other than cosmetic ones, and the city's permit guide lists what counts. Work done without a permit can come up when a buyer or lender reviews the house, so check your own records first.

  • Permit needed: basement and bathroom alterations, decks, new window or door openings, furnace installs, plumbing and electrical work, structural roofing changes, and a water heater that changes between gas and electric.
  • No permit needed: new flooring, kitchen cabinet replacement, residential siding, exact window replacement, and a same-type water heater swap.
  • Rental houses: a licensed contractor must pull the permit and do the work.

An owner who lives in the house may pull permits and do the work. Fences over 50 feet and sheds over 50 square feet need permits, while smaller ones do not, although zoning setbacks still apply. A house in a regulated floodplain may also require an itemized list of improvements. If your property is in a historic district, you also need a certificate of appropriateness, so call Inspections and Enforcement at 920-448-3300 to find out. On one- and two-family jobs, the city's residential permit page says it verifies that the contracting business holds the state Dwelling Contractor Certification and Qualifier Certification before it issues a permit.

What happens to a Green Bay short-term rental permit when I sell?

The permit does not transfer. Green Bay's short-term rental rules cover any stay under 28 consecutive days, and the city's application page states that the permit is non-transferable if the property is sold. A new owner has to apply on their own.

The initial application costs $500 and a renewal costs $250. A permit runs from July 1 through June 30, and renewals open on April 1. Missing the June 30 deadline voids the permit. Applicants submit proof of registration for Brown County room tax, a Brown County Health Department inspection report, proof of insurance and a local representative who is within 30 minutes of the property. The city says review can take up to 14 business days.

If you are selling a house that has run as a rental, tell your buyer which of those steps are current. A buyer who plans to continue the rental should budget the fee and the timeline.

What must a Green Bay seller disclose to the buyer?

An owner of a one- to four-unit property must deliver a completed condition report to the buyer within 10 days after the contract is accepted, as Wisconsin Statutes chapter 709 requires. A buyer who gets it late can rescind within two business days after the 10 days run out.

The report is a disclosure and not a warranty. It defines a defect as a condition that has a significant adverse effect on value, significantly impairs health or safety, or would shorten the expected life of the premises if left unrepaired. If you are a court-appointed fiduciary who never lived in the house, you are excused. Sellers answering for a long-owned or inherited house should still read each question and answer from what they know.

How do I record the sale in Brown County and what is the transfer fee?

The seller owes a transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value, set by Wisconsin Statutes 77.22. A $200,000 sale carries a $600 fee. The register collects it when the deed is submitted for recording, along with an electronic transfer return signed by both sides.

Green Bay deeds go to the Brown County Register of Deeds in the Northern Building, Room 260, at 305 E. Walnut Street, phone 920-448-4470. Its posted hours for walk-in recordings are 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday and 7:30 to 10:30 a.m. on Friday. The mailing address is P.O. Box 23600, Green Bay, WI 54305-3600. Ask the Brown County treasurer for the tax figures your closing agent needs to prorate the bill.

Do I have to make repairs before selling a house in Green Bay?

No. A seller can sell as is, and a cash buyer accepts the house in its present condition. You still must fill out the state condition report truthfully, and open permits or code orders should be cleared up or disclosed.

Does Green Bay require a permit to replace siding?

Residential siding does not need a permit according to the city's permit guide, but roofing with structural changes, decks and furnace installs do. Call 920-448-3300 to confirm for your project.

Can a buyer keep my Green Bay short-term rental permit?

No. The permit is non-transferable when the property is sold, so the buyer has to apply for a new one and pay the $500 initial fee.

Who pays the Wisconsin transfer fee?

The seller pays it at 30 cents per $100 of value, and the Brown County Register of Deeds collects it at recording. Some transfers, such as those by will or descent, are exempt.

How long do I have to give the buyer the condition report?

Within 10 days after the contract is accepted. If the buyer gets it late, the buyer has two business days after that period to rescind and recover deposits.

What is it like to sell a house in Appleton, Wisconsin?

Appleton is the county seat of Outagamie County and the sixth most populous city in Wisconsin, with a Census Bureau estimate of 75,452 residents on July 1, 2025. It sits on the Fox River north of Lake Winnebago, about 30 miles southwest of Green Bay and 100 miles north of Milwaukee. The city covers about 24.8 square miles of land, and most of it lies in Outagamie County, with small parts in Calumet and Winnebago counties.

Paper mills drove the city's growth after the first one opened in 1853, and the Vulcan Street Plant on the Fox River began operating in 1882 as the first hydroelectric central station in the country. Appleton was incorporated as a city on March 2, 1857. The economy has since added retail and health care, and St. Elizabeth Hospital, ThedaCare Regional Medical Center in Appleton, Lawrence University and Fox Valley Technical College are among the larger institutions.

Appleton has a humid continental climate, with warm to hot summers and cold winters. Recorded temperatures range from 107 degrees Fahrenheit in 1936 to minus 32 in 1929. Wikipedia also records an EF3 tornado that struck Appleton on July 27, 2026, with damage in the city and neighboring Menasha. If your house took storm damage, say so on the condition report and keep your insurance and repair records together.

Which schools, hospitals and roads matter to Appleton buyers?

The Appleton Area School District serves the city, and its main public high schools are Appleton East, Appleton North and Appleton West. Catholic Xavier High School and Fox Valley Lutheran High School are the two parochial high schools.

  • Valley Transit, owned by the city, runs bus lines across the Fox Valley, and Lamers Bus Lines connects to Wausau, Oshkosh, Fond du Lac and Milwaukee.
  • Appleton International Airport is about six miles west of downtown.
  • Rail freight runs on Canadian National lines. There is no intercity passenger rail.
  • Two hospitals serve the city, St. Elizabeth and ThedaCare Regional Medical Center.

Several communities near Appleton use an Appleton mailing address without being inside the city, including the Town of Grand Chute and the Village of Harrison. The city's inspection office warns owners to confirm the address is within city limits before buying a permit.

Do I need permits or an inspection before selling in Appleton?

Work you do to get a house ready for sale may need a permit. Building Inspections says decks, remodeling, pools, siding and sheds over 50 square feet most likely need one. When you are unsure, call (920) 832-6411 before starting. Morning in-office hours at City Hall run from 8:00 a.m. to 9:30 a.m. on weekdays.

Homeowners can pull permits for a single-family home they own and occupy, but they follow the same rules as a contractor. Residential contractors must be registered with the State, and the city suggests asking for their registration number. An unfinished inspection leaves a permit open, which can lead to a re-inspection fee later.

If you inherited a house that has been neglected, know that the city can cut grass and clear debris after a complaint, and it may need inspection warrants to do so. Building Inspections also offers a free courtesy inspection that lists what would bring a building into compliance.

Setbacks for one- and two-family lots differ by zoning. In R-1A and R-1B the side setback is 8 feet and 6 feet, and the rear setback is 25 feet in each of R-1A, R-1B, R-1C and R-2. Check them before you promise a buyer a garage or addition.

How does the Appleton assessor handle a sold house?

The Assessor's Office inspects recently sold homes each fall and winter, so a letter about your sale is possible, and the office offers online scheduling for it. Wisconsin's assessment manual tells assessors to make reasonable attempts to view sale properties. The office also inspects houses with building permits and reviews online listings for work done without one.

Appleton revalues all property at least once every five years and tries to inspect each property at least once in ten. The assessor's phone number is (920) 832-5850. For 2026 the Board of Review adjourned on April 29, 2026, so the 2026 assessments are final. The 2026 schedule had notices mailed April 9, open book from April 13 to 22 and the board on April 29. Ask the assessor in spring for the next dates, and call the City Clerk's Office at (920) 832-6443 to file a formal objection.

The assessor's page adds a point many owners miss: when the bill arrives in December it is too late to object, and paying under protest does not count unless you first filed with the Board of Review.

How are Appleton property taxes paid, and what happens at a sale?

Appleton lets owners pay in four installments, due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. A late payment cancels the installment option and adds monthly interest on the unpaid balance, as state law requires. After the final installment, outstanding balances are delinquent and go to the county treasurer for the county where the parcel sits.

  • Pay in person at City Hall, 100 N. Appleton St., weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or use the night deposit box.
  • Mail checks to the City of Appleton at P.O. Box 2519, Appleton, WI 54912-2519.
  • Pay online with a card or e-check using the parcel number. The payment vendor charges a convenience fee that the city does not receive.
  • For delinquent bills, call Outagamie County at (920) 832-5065, Calumet County at (920) 849-1457 or Winnebago County at (920) 232-3420.

Ask the City Finance Department, (920) 832-6442, for the paid-to-date figure before closing, and give it to the title company. Refunds over $750, and any refund for a payment made by mail or drop box, are mailed within four to six weeks.

What are the recording and transfer steps in Appleton?

Complete a Wisconsin Real Estate Transfer Return on the Department of Revenue website, print the receipt, and bring it with the deed and fees to the Register of Deeds. Under s. 77.22(1), a completed return and fee collection are prerequisites to recording. For most of Appleton that office is the Outagamie County Register of Deeds. If your parcel is in the Calumet or Winnebago portion, record there instead.

Outagamie charges $30 for a standard real estate document and stops recording at 4:00 p.m. Documents need a 3 inch by 3 inch blank space in the upper right corner, a parcel number, a complete legal description, notarized signatures and the name of the person who drafted the document.

Sellers of one to four unit homes also owe the buyer a real estate condition report within 10 days after the offer is accepted, or the buyer may rescind under s. 709.02.

Can I rent out my Appleton house before it sells?

A stay shorter than a month is a short-term rental, and Appleton licenses it as a tourist rooming house through the Health Department. The owner needs a license before offering the stay, a pre-inspection and an annual health inspection. Licenses renew on July 1 and expire June 30. The Health Department's number is 920-832-6429.

Hosts who rent on their own must collect state and county sales tax and register with the Department of Revenue when total sales revenue reaches $2,000, and they must collect local room tax.

What are my choices if I want to sell fast in Appleton?

You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept a cash offer. A listing opens the house to the widest set of buyers but depends on showings, inspections and the condition report. Selling yourself saves a commission and means handling the contract, disclosure and paperwork alone. A cash buyer can close on a shorter timeline and buy the house as is, which suits inherited homes, tenants in place or repairs you cannot afford.

How fast can I sell my house in Appleton, WI?

The timeline depends on the route you pick and on how soon the title, tax balance and condition report are ready. A listing adds time for showings and the buyer's financing, and every sale of a one to four unit home needs the condition report within 10 days after the offer is accepted.

Who do I pay Appleton property taxes to?

The City of Appleton Finance Department takes payments through the final installment on July 31. After that, balances are delinquent and go to the county treasurer for Outagamie, Calumet or Winnebago County, depending on where the parcel is.

Does Appleton require an inspection before I sell?

No inspection is required to sell. Permits may be required for work you do first, such as decks, siding, remodeling and sheds over 50 square feet. Call Building Inspections at (920) 832-6411 if you are unsure.

What does it cost to record a deed in Appleton?

The Outagamie County Register of Deeds charges $30 for a standard real estate document. You also complete a Real Estate Transfer Return with the Department of Revenue, and any transfer fee due is paid when the deed is recorded.

Can I list my Appleton house as a vacation rental?

Yes, with a Tourist Rooming House License from the Appleton Health Department. A pre-inspection is required, and licenses renew each July 1. Call 920-832-6429 to schedule the inspection.

What should you know before selling a house in Eau Claire, WI?

Eau Claire is the seat of Eau Claire County, with a Census Bureau estimate of 72,465 residents on July 1, 2025, up 4.4% from the 2020 base. It is a renter-heavy city, so many sales involve tenants, small multifamily buildings or houses near the university.

You can sell by listing, by owner, or to a cash buyer. The steps that decide how smoothly it goes are the same in each case: city permit records, the assessment and tax calendar, the seller disclosure report, and recording the deed with the county.

How did Eau Claire's history shape its housing?

The city sits where the Eau Claire and Chippewa rivers meet. The first permanent settlers arrived in 1845, the city was incorporated in 1872, and it began as three separate settlements: the downtown village, West Eau Claire and Shawtown. Lumber mills built the early economy, and by the 1950s the built-up area had spread east to meet Altoona, according to the city's Wikipedia entry.

Two later events changed the housing picture. The University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire opened in 1916 and moved the economy toward education, health care and manufacturing. In 1991 the Uniroyal tire plant announced its closure, which cost 1,358 jobs, and the complex is now Banbury Place, a small business incubator. A 1982 survey identified the Randall Park, Third Ward and Emery Street Bungalow historic districts, most of which reached the National Register in 1983, so older bungalows and large lumber-era houses are part of the resale market.

Part of the city lies in Chippewa County, not only Eau Claire County. If your parcel is on that side of the line, ask which county's Register of Deeds and treasurer handle your recording and tax bill.

Which schools serve Eau Claire neighborhoods?

The Eau Claire Area School District lists Memorial High School, North High School and McKinley Secondary School, three middle schools (DeLong, Northstar and South) and a long list of elementary schools that includes Flynn, Lakeshore, Locust Lane, Longfellow, Manz, Meadowview, Northwoods, Putnam Heights, Robbins, Roosevelt, Sam Davey and Sherman.

Ask the district office which school a given address feeds before you advertise the house, and do the same for parcels near the edge of the city, which may sit in a different district.

How does Eau Claire assess property and collect tax?

The City of Eau Claire sets a January 1 assessment date, and the tax bill is due in full January 31 or in two installments on January 31 and July 31. Assessment change notices usually go out between the end of April and the end of May, and the Board of Review meets during a 45-day window that opens on the fourth Monday in April.

  • Talk to an assessor first. The city says that informal meeting shows how your value was set.
  • If you still disagree, you can appeal the Board's decision to the Department of Revenue within 20 days of receiving it, with a $100 filing fee, when the value in dispute is $1 million or less.
  • A court appeal must be made within 90 days after the Board of Review adjourns, and it is decided on the record from your hearing.

The assessor's office is at 715-839-4926, and property records are searchable through the city's Beacon tool. Because tax is billed for the whole year, your closing will prorate it between you and the buyer, and the title company can show the split. Ask the Eau Claire County treasurer for the status of any unpaid bill on the parcel.

What permit and rental rules apply to Eau Claire houses?

The city's Inspection Services Division reviews plans, issues permits and inspects construction and remodeling work covering building, heating, air conditioning, electrical and plumbing. It also enforces ordinances on floodplain, zoning, property upkeep and land use. Inspection requests run through the Evolve portal or by phone, not by email to individual inspectors.

Short-term rentals have a separate set of rules that affect how a buyer can use the house. On December 10, 2024 the City Council created Chapter 5.66 and a Short-Term Rental License.

  • An owner applies first for a Tourist Rooming House license through the city-county Health Department (715-839-4718).
  • The city license is reviewed by Planning and Zoning (715-839-4914), with a parking count, a building plan and a trash container sketch.
  • The initial review fee is $700 and the annual renewal is $300, and licenses run from June 30 to June 30.
  • The council removed the proposed seven-night minimum and 180-day annual cap.

If your house has operated as a short-term rental, confirm the license status with Planning before you list, since buyers who want to continue the use will ask.

How do you transfer a deed in Eau Claire County?

Deeds are recorded with the Eau Claire County Register of Deeds, which files deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, plats and certified survey maps. Since January 1, 2025 a postage-paid envelope has to be supplied for the return of paper documents. The county's land records page lists forms, the electronic transfer return, a checklist for recording and a filing fee schedule, so check the current fee there or at rod@eauclairecounty.gov.

Wis. Stat. 77.22 charges the grantor 30 cents for each $100 of value, and the register collects it when the deed is submitted. The register has no duty to check the value you report. For a gift or a deed with nominal consideration, Wis. Stat. 77.21 uses the estimated open-market price, which matters when a family member buys at a discount.

What does the Wisconsin seller disclosure require in Eau Claire?

Chapter 709 requires owners of one-to-four-unit property to give the buyer a completed condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. In a condominium sale the owner also supplies an addendum with condominium information at the same time. A buyer who does not receive the report can rescind within two business days after the 10 days run out and recover deposits.

Personal representatives, trustees, conservators and court-supervised fiduciaries who never lived in the house are excused. The excusal is limited to those fiduciaries, so an ordinary owner, including a landlord, completes the report.

Is a cash sale or a listing better in Eau Claire?

A listing works when the house shows well and you can handle showings and a lender's timeline. A cash sale fits a house with deferred repairs, a tenant in place, a probate timeline or a payoff date.

Ask for a net sheet with any offer. It should list the loan payoff, the $3 per $1,000 transfer fee, recording, prorated tax and repair credits, so the offers compare on proceeds.

Who records deeds for Eau Claire properties?

The Eau Claire County Register of Deeds records them. Provide a postage-paid return envelope for paper documents, and check the county's filing fee schedule before you submit.

When are Eau Claire property taxes due?

January 31 in full, or in two installments on January 31 and July 31. The assessment date is January 1.

How much is the transfer fee on an Eau Claire sale?

It is 30 cents per $100 of value, paid by the seller under Wis. Stat. 77.22. A $250,000 sale carries a $750 fee.

Do I need a license to run a short-term rental in Eau Claire?

Yes. Eau Claire requires a Tourist Rooming House license from the Health Department and a city Short-Term Rental License, with a $700 initial review fee and a $300 annual renewal.

Can I appeal my Eau Claire assessment after the Board of Review?

Yes. You can appeal to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue within 20 days of the decision, with a $100 filing fee, or to circuit court within 90 days after the Board adjourns.

Fond du Lac is the seat of Fond du Lac County and sits at the southern end of Lake Winnebago, which is how it got its French name meaning the bottom of the lake. Wikipedia lists the city's area as 20.54 square miles, of which 19.23 are land. The east and west branches of the Fond du Lac River join inside the city and flow into the lake near Lakeside Park, a recreation area of more than 400 acres.

The first railroad reached the community in 1852, and logging and milling drove its growth in the late 1800s. The city has four historic districts: South Main Street, North Main Street, Linden Street, and East Division and Sheboygan Streets, plus about 20 listings on the National Register of Historic Places. The state transfer fee is 30 cents per $100 of value, and it is owed by the seller under section 77.22. On a $175,000 sale, the fee is $525. Brookfield is a city in eastern Waukesha County with an estimated 41,448 residents as of July 1, 2025, so a sale here is shaped by suburban Milwaukee-area rules and a housing stock that is mostly owner-occupied. You can list with an agent, sell on your own, or sell to a cash buyer, and the steps below apply to all three.

The items that move a Brookfield closing most are the permit history of the house, the property tax calendar, the seller's disclosure report, and the recording of the deed at the Waukesha County Register of Deeds. Each is covered below with the office to call.

What is Brookfield like for a home seller?

Brookfield was cut out of the old Town of Brookfield and incorporated as a city on August 14, 1954. At that point it had about 7,900 residents and 17.5 square miles. It now covers roughly 27.7 square miles, and the remaining piece of the town still sits along the city's western edge, according to the city's Wikipedia entry.

Postwar subdivisions drove most of that growth. The first suburban plat, Kinsey's Garvendale, dates to 1928, and building picked up after the Second World War. For a seller that history matters in a practical way: much of the housing stock dates from the postwar growth, so aging furnaces, roofs, windows and electrical panels are common repair questions from buyers.

The city has four ZIP codes (53005, 53008, 53045 and 53072) and a subcontinental divide that runs near Calhoun Road and Capitol Drive. Water east of the divide drains toward Lake Michigan, and water west of it drains toward the Fox River of Illinois and Wisconsin. The City of Brookfield mails real estate tax bills around December 15 each year. The city collects for itself, the school district, Waukesha County and Waukesha County Technical College on one combined bill. How the current year's tax is split between you and the buyer is set in the purchase contract and worked out by the title company. Ask the title company for the proration figure before closing, and ask the Brookfield Treasurer at 262-787-3513 about the status of any open bill.

What does it take to transfer title in Waukesha County?

A deed has to be recorded with the Waukesha County Register of Deeds, and Wisconsin attaches a transfer fee to most sales. Under Wis. Stat. 77.22 the grantor pays 30 cents for each $100 of value, which works out to $900 on a $300,000 sale. A Real Estate Transfer Return signed by both sides has to be filed electronically with the Department of Revenue before the register will accept the deed.

The county's recording fee for a standard deed is $30, and the county accepts payment by check or money order only. A document that is eRecorded comes back right away. A paper document returns the same day if you supply an email address, or in two to three weeks if you provide a stamped envelope. Separately, Chapter 709 requires most sellers to give the buyer a completed real estate condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. Should you sell to a cash buyer or list in Brookfield?

How do I sell a house fast in Franklin, WI?

The fastest route is a cash sale, which skips the buyer's mortgage approval, and the slowest is a listing that waits on showings and a lender. Franklin sellers can also sell on their own, so the real question is how much time and repair work you can absorb.

  • Agent listing: a good fit for a well-kept house when you can wait for the best financed offer.
  • Owner sale: you handle the pricing, showings, contract and state disclosure form.
  • Cash buyer: a fit for a house with deferred maintenance, a divorce or estate sale, a move on a deadline, or a rental you no longer want to manage.

Franklin is a city where most homes are owner-occupied. The Census Bureau puts the rate at 77.3 percent for 2020-2024, so a typical seller here owns a house they have lived in. Nearly one resident in five, 19.6 percent, is 65 or older, so estate and downsizing sales are a regular part of the local picture.

What should a seller know about Franklin's layout and history?

Franklin is a city in southern Milwaukee County that borders Oak Creek to the east, Greendale, Hales Corners and Greenfield to the north, Racine County to the south and Waukesha County to the west. Wikipedia gives its land area as 34.58 square miles, and the Root River runs south through the city and divides it.

The Town of Franklin was split off from the Town of Kinnikinick on December 20, 1839, and was named for Benjamin Franklin. By the 1950s it was known as a City of Homes because of its growing residential neighborhoods. Town officials feared Milwaukee might annex part of their land, so they incorporated Franklin as a fourth-class city on August 15, 1956.

The city sits about four miles from Milwaukee Mitchell International Airport and close to Interstate 94. U.S. Highway 45 and Wisconsin highways 36, 100 and 241 pass through it. When you describe your house to a buyer, say where it sits relative to those roads, the Root River and the airport, since location is part of what any buyer will weigh.

What do the Franklin housing numbers show?

Franklin has the highest household income of the four cities in this group, and its median home value is $364,200. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page is the source for the table below.

What work on a Franklin house needs a permit?

Franklin requires a permit to build a new structure, add to a house, make structural changes, and for a long list of other jobs. The city's Inspection Services FAQ names accessory buildings, residing, reroofing, fences, decks, swimming pools and HVAC. Permits must be in hand before work starts.

  • Electrical and plumbing work must be done by licensed contractors who pull their own permits.
  • A homeowner can do other work, but the owner is responsible for the permit even if a contractor was supposed to get it.
  • Residential permits are processed in the order received, and the city asks you to allow at least 10 business days. Contractors applying for one- and two-family work must hold valid state certifications.

If a past contractor never pulled a permit, call Inspection Services at 414-425-0084. The office is at 9229 W. Loomis Road and is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Staff will help you obtain the required permits and inspections, though the city cannot settle a dispute between you and the contractor.

If you plan fixes before listing, remember the noise rule in the city code: operating tools or equipment between 9 p.m. and 7 a.m. is a violation when it creates a noise disturbance. A cash buyer may take the house without those fixes, which can save you the time of managing contractors.

What disclosures must a Franklin seller provide?

A Franklin seller must give the buyer a real estate condition report within 10 days after an offer is accepted, and a buyer who does not receive it can rescind. This comes from Wisconsin Statutes chapter 709, which applies to property with one to four dwelling units.

The buyer may rescind within two business days after the 10-day period ends and is entitled to a refund of deposits. If the property is a condominium unit, you must also attach an addendum that names the condominium and its association, lists current assessments and special charges, and says whether they have been paid. A personal representative, trustee or conservator who never occupied the house is not required to complete the report.

Sellers often ask whether a cash sale changes any of this. The statute applies to any sale, exchange or land contract of that kind of property, and it does not turn on how the buyer pays. If the transfer is exempt from the state transfer fee, such as an inheritance by will, the report is excused as well.

How is a Franklin sale recorded and what is the transfer fee?

The deed is recorded with the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds, 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, Milwaukee, and the seller pays a state transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value. On a $350,000 sale the fee is $1,050. The statute behind it is section 77.22.

The county's recording page says each document costs $30 to record, and every conveyance needs an electronic transfer return receipt. The office accepts cash, checks or money orders, but not credit or debit cards. Documents are recorded in order of receipt within three to five business days, and the original is mailed back in one to two weeks. For recording questions, call 414-278-4005. For help with the transfer return, call the Department of Revenue at 608-266-1594.

If you inherited a Franklin house, a transfer by will or descent is exempt from the fee under section 77.25. The register's office does not supply deed forms and cannot give legal advice, so use an attorney or title company to prepare the paperwork. When a spouse has died and both names are on the deed, the county describes a Termination of Decedent's Interest form, recorded with a $30 fee and a transfer return that claims the 77.25 (11) exemption. Ask the Milwaukee County treasurer for the tax balance so your closing agent can prorate it.

What is the fastest way to sell a house in Franklin?

A cash sale is usually the fastest, because the buyer does not need a lender's approval. A listing takes longer since it depends on showings, offers, inspections and financing.

Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Franklin?

Yes. The city lists reroofing among the work that needs a permit, along with siding, fences, decks, pools and HVAC. Call Inspection Services at 414-425-0084 to confirm what applies.

Where do I record a deed for a Franklin property?

At the Milwaukee County Register of Deeds, 901 N. 9th Street, Room 103, Milwaukee. Bring the original deed, the electronic transfer return receipt and the $30 recording fee.

How much is the Wisconsin real estate transfer fee?

It is 30 cents for each $100 of value, paid by the seller. Some transfers are exempt, including transfers by will or descent.

Can I sell an inherited house in Franklin without living in it?

Yes. A court-appointed personal representative or trustee who never occupied the house does not have to complete the condition report. Use a deed and the electronic transfer return, and ask the register of deeds how to clear a deceased owner's name from title.

What kind of city is Beloit, Wisconsin for a home seller?

Beloit is a Rock County city on the Rock River at the Illinois state line, with about 36,600 residents and 17.3 square miles of land. The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 36,649, a little below the 36,966 counted in 2010. Settlers from New Hampshire platted the village in 1838 on level ground with water power from Turtle Creek, and the founders planned wide streets on the New England model. The place was first called New Albany before the name Beloit was adopted in 1838.

Fairbanks-Morse Defense, ABC Supply, PlayMonster and Regal Beloit are among the companies headquartered here, and Union Pacific still serves the Fairbanks-Morse plant. Downtown Beloit was one of the two inaugural Wisconsin Main Street communities. The city won a Great American Main Street Award in 2011, and loft and hotel conversions such as the Ironworks Hotel, Hotel Goodwin and the Wright and Wagner Lofts have added downtown housing and lodging.

Historic buildings in Beloit include the Fairbanks Flats, built in 1917, and the Lathrop-Munn Cobblestone House. If your own house is old, expect buyers to ask about the roof, wiring and plumbing, and have your repair records ready.

Beloit homes are worth far less than the county median, and fewer households own their homes. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $156,500, against $231,600 for Rock County as a whole, and the city owner-occupied rate is 59.4%, against 71.2% countywide.

Which schools, colleges and roads matter in Beloit?

The School District of Beloit serves about 5,923 students across six primary schools, two intermediate schools and one high school, Beloit Memorial High School. Parts of the Beloit area are served by the Beloit Turner School District instead, so check the district listed for a parcel before you advertise it.

  • Beloit College, a private liberal arts college with about 1,300 undergraduates, sits in the city, and its Middle College is the oldest academic building in Wisconsin still in use.
  • Blackhawk Technical College runs a campus in Beloit.
  • Beloit Transit and Van Galder Bus Company provide bus service.
  • Beloit Airport is a general aviation field inside the city, and Southern Wisconsin Regional Airport lies north of it in Rock County.

Do I need a permit or inspection to sell a Beloit house?

A building permit is required for new structures, additions, renovations, structural repair and mechanical system replacement, and a Certificate of Occupancy follows once the work is inspected. That rule is from the city's Planning and Building pages. Site plan review applies to new structures, additions and parking lot expansions, and architectural review applies to most buildings except homes with one or two units.

Finish any permitted repairs before you list so the work has passed inspection.

Rentals have their own oversight. The city's Community and Housing Services Division enforces the Housing Property Maintenance Code, performs interior rental inspections and does multi-family fire inspections. If you own a Beloit rental and plan to sell with or without tenants, call that division before you list and ask about the inspection status of the unit. It also runs housing rehabilitation loan programs that may fit repairs you cannot afford up front.

How is a Beloit house assessed, and when can I object?

The City of Beloit contracts with Tyler Technologies as City Assessor and has since 2014. The assessor's office is part of the process that produces your tax bill, and the roll is posted each spring. For 2026, open book ran April 20 to 23 and April 27, and the Board of Review held its first meeting on May 20, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. in the Forum of City Hall. Those dates have passed. Call the assessor at 608-364-6670 in the spring to confirm the next ones.

  • To file a notice of intent to object, call the City Clerk-Treasurer at 608-364-6682 with your name, address, parcel number and phone number.
  • Give notice at least 48 hours before the first Board of Review meeting.
  • File a written objection with your own estimate of the land and improvement values in the first two hours of that meeting.
  • Object to the total of land and improvements, not to one of them alone.

The city's process page lists three steps: talk to the assessor, attend open book, then ask for a Board of Review hearing. After the board, the appeal routes in the Department of Revenue's Guide for Property Owners apply.

How are Beloit property taxes paid before a sale?

Beloit owners can pay in four installments, and every payment goes to the Rock County Treasurer. The due dates are January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. Unpaid taxes become delinquent and carry interest of 1.5% per month from February 1, with part of a month counting as a whole month. A missed installment makes the whole remaining balance delinquent.

The Treasurer is at 51 South Main Street, Janesville, WI 53545, open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The phone number is 608-757-5670. Card payments go through GovTech Services at 2.29% for credit, $3.95 for debit and $1.00 for an e-check. Beloit address changes go to the Treasurer's Office, not to Real Property.

Before closing, request the paid-to-date and balance figures for your parcel in writing and give them to the title company. If a mortgage lender pays from escrow, confirm what it has paid. The county says any escrow overpayment returns to the escrow company when the company sends the payment, and the owner gets it when the owner pays in person.

What are the recording and transfer steps in Beloit?

Beloit parcels are recorded with the Rock County Register of Deeds, which takes walk-in visitors and keeps a drop box in the Courthouse lobby. Wisconsin requires a completed Real Estate Transfer Return from the Department of Revenue website. Under s. 77.22(1), the return and the fee collection come before a deed can be accepted for recording.

The Rock County Treasurer says its records reflect the most recently recorded document, so the buyer's name appears on later tax bills only after the deed is recorded.

The seller's real estate condition report is due to the buyer within 10 days after acceptance of the contract (s. 709.02). If you learn something before acceptance that changes an answer on the form, s. 709.035 requires an amended report within 10 days of acceptance. The form has sections on structural and mechanical items and on taxes, special assessments and permits.

What are my options for selling a house fast in Beloit?

Beloit sellers can list on the open market, sell on their own, or take a cash offer. Listing reaches the most buyers and suits a house in good shape. A cash buyer buys the house as is, which helps with inherited property, a tenant in place or repairs that would cost more than you want to spend. Whichever route you choose, settle the property tax balance and complete the condition report. Ask the closing agent for a written estimate of what you will net before you accept an offer.

Where do I pay property tax on a Beloit house?

Pay the Rock County Treasurer, 51 South Main Street, Janesville. Every City of Beloit installment goes to the county, due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. Call 608-757-5670 with questions.

How much is the Beloit median home value?

The Census Bureau lists $156,500 as the median value of owner-occupied homes in Beloit for 2020 to 2024. Rock County's median is $231,600.

Does Beloit inspect rental houses before a sale?

The city's Community and Housing Services Division performs interior rental inspections and enforces the Housing Property Maintenance Code. Call the division before you list a rental to ask about the status of the unit.

When can I protest my Beloit assessment?

In the spring, after the assessment roll opens for open book. The 2026 Board of Review met on May 20, 2026, and that date has passed. Call the City Clerk-Treasurer at 608-364-6682 for the next notice-of-intent process.

What documents does a Beloit seller need to give the buyer?

A completed real estate condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted, plus a Real Estate Transfer Return filed with the Department of Revenue for recording. Your deed is recorded with the Rock County Register of Deeds.

That price level means a few thousand dollars of deferred repair can be a large share of the sale price, which is why many sellers here weigh an as-is sale against fixing the house first.

What is Manitowoc, Wisconsin like?

Manitowoc is the seat of Manitowoc County, on Lake Michigan at the mouth of the Manitowoc River. It is 24 miles from Sheboygan, 34 miles from Green Bay, 39 miles from Appleton and 74 miles from Milwaukee. The city covers about 18 square miles, and the 2020 Census counted 34,626 residents.

The area was chartered as a village in 1851 and incorporated as a city in 1870. Shipbuilding began with schooners in the 1840s and later produced landing craft, tankers and submarines in World War II, and the National Park Service named Manitowoc a World War II Heritage City in December 2022. The Wisconsin Maritime Museum is here, and the SS Badger ferry sails from Manitowoc to Ludington, Michigan.

Two older neighborhoods keep their names: Alverno, near the I-43 business park on the west side, and Kellners Corners, a residential area on the northwest side along Rapids Road. Lake Michigan moderates the weather, with milder winters and cooler summers than nearby inland cities, and the city averages 31.17 inches of precipitation a year, with snow most common from December through March.

Who employs people in Manitowoc, and where do children go to school?

Manufacturing still anchors the local economy. Lakeside Foods has its world headquarters in the city, and Burger Boat Company builds yachts here. Baileigh Industrial and Orion Energy Systems are other employers, and Manitowoc Ice, now owned by Pentair, still manufactures in town. Holy Family Memorial and Aurora Health Care run the main medical networks in the county.

The Manitowoc Public School District serves the city, with Lincoln High School as the public high school, and Roncalli High School and Manitowoc Lutheran High School as private options. The University of Wisconsin-Green Bay Manitowoc Campus and Lakeshore Technical College are both inside the city limits. I-43 connects north to Green Bay and south to Sheboygan and Milwaukee, and US 10, US 151 and WIS 42 cross the area. Maritime Metro Transit runs buses in Manitowoc and Two Rivers.

Do Manitowoc landlords have to register a rental before selling?

The registration belongs to the present owner, and a change of ownership requires a new registration by the buyer.

  • New rental units must be registered within 30 days of occupancy.
  • Contact changes must be reported within 30 days.
  • Missing the deadline can bring a forfeiture of up to $100 per rental unit, and each week of noncompliance counts as a separate offense.
  • Buildings with three or more units continue to receive an annual common-area inspection from the Fire Department.

Registration forms go to Building Inspection at 900 Quay Street, and the department answers questions at (920) 686-6940. Even a vacant duplex has to be registered, so bring the paperwork current before a buyer asks for it.

What about a short-term rental or an unfinished permit?

A short-term rental is handled separately from a standard rental. The city does not require rental registration for a tourist rooming house, which is licensed by the Manitowoc County Health Department instead, at (920) 683-4155. Short-term rentals are a permitted use in zoning districts R-1 through R-7 and B-1, and room tax questions go to the city Finance Department at (920) 686-6960.

Open permits matter at closing. The city asks you to give 24 hours' notice on business days to schedule an inspection, and a project whose permit expires without a final inspection is archived as incomplete, with the work deemed unapproved. If a deck, furnace or bathroom was done under a permit that was never finaled, call Building Inspection before you list so the buyer does not find it first.

The required inspections are listed on each permit. For building work, the city's inspection types are:

  • Footing, before the concrete pour.
  • Foundation, before backfilling.
  • Rough in, before insulation or drywall covers the framing.
  • Insulation, on installed insulation and vapor retarders.
  • Final and final occupancy, which verify code compliance before the space is used.

How do assessments and the Board of Review work in Manitowoc?

The City Assessor values property as of January 1 under Chapter 70 of the Wisconsin Statutes, and the city contracts Associated Appraisal Consultants to do the work. The city's 2026 revaluation schedule put the Open Book sessions on May 19 and June 2 and the Board of Review on June 10, 2026 at 5 p.m. in the Council Chambers at City Hall. Those dates have passed, so any challenge to the 2026 value is already closed for this year.

The Assessor sets neither tax rates nor collects tax, and the city says it adjusts values to market using open sales every other year. If you receive a letter asking to verify property details, answer it, because the same data feeds your valuation when you sell.

What are the Wisconsin steps and recording details for a Manitowoc sale?

The seller owes a transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value under Wis. Stat. 77.22, and at the Manitowoc median of $160,700 that comes to about $482. Wis. Stat. 709.02 requires an owner of a one-to-four unit property to give the buyer a condition report within 10 days after the contract is accepted, or the buyer may rescind. The report form includes a section on wells, septic systems and storage tanks, so gather that information early if your lot is outside city services.

The deed is recorded with the Manitowoc County Register of Deeds in the Courthouse at 1010 S 8th Street, Room 107, which is open Monday 8:30 to 5:00 and Tuesday through Friday 8:30 to 4:30. The transfer return itself is filed electronically through the Department of Revenue, and you bring the printed receipt with the signed deed.

What is Muskego like, and how did the city develop?

Muskego is a city in Waukesha County and part of the Milwaukee metropolitan area. Its name comes from a Potawatomi word meaning sunfish. The first European arrived in 1827, the Potawatomi ceded their Wisconsin lands in 1833, and the Luther Parker family from New Hampshire became the first permanent settlers. A largely agricultural area for generations, Muskego was incorporated as a city in 1964 and has grown through new housing developments into a bedroom community for Milwaukee. It also has a large Norwegian American population.

The city has about 36 square miles in total, of which 4.38 square miles is water. Density is low, at roughly 792 people per square mile in 2020, and 20.7 percent of residents are 65 or older. The Tess Corners Fire Department, a volunteer department, serves the city.

How do Muskego's lakes affect a home sale?

Three lakes lie inside city limits, and the lake a house faces shapes the questions buyers ask. Big Muskego Lake covers about 2,260 acres in the south-central part of the city and is shallow, with cattail marsh along its edges. Little Muskego Lake is 506 acres, reaches 65 feet at its deepest, and most of its shoreline is developed with houses. Lake Denoon covers 162 acres in the southwest.

  • Waterfront buyers ask about shoreline rules, so gather your survey, any pier or retaining-wall records and permits.
  • Big Muskego Lake is mostly under four feet deep with a muck bottom, while Little Muskego Lake averages 14 feet, so describe the lake your house sits on accurately.
  • Little Muskego Lake hosts boating, skiing, sailing and fishing, which many waterfront buyers want to hear about.

For questions about work near the water, call the Building Inspection Division at (262) 679-4145 before you promise a buyer anything about what can be built or changed.

Which schools serve Muskego houses?

The Muskego-Norway School District serves the city. Its schools include Bay Lane, Lakeview (which serves Muskego residents but sits in the Town of Norway) and Mill Valley elementary schools, Muskego Lakes Middle School and Lake Denoon Middle School, and Muskego High School. Two parochial options are St. Leonard K-8 Catholic School and St. Paul's Evangelical Lutheran Grade School.

The council adopted the chapter on April 12, 2022.

  • Each license runs January 1 through December 31 and is renewed yearly.
  • The owner must carry liability insurance and be reachable from 8:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. on rental days.
  • Guests must sign a register, and a unit cannot be rented to more than one party within a six-day period.

A buyer who plans to keep renting should ask the City Clerk about applying for a license in their own name. Clear any unpaid city charges first, since the chapter bars issuing or renewing a license with money owed to the city.

The condition report rule in Wis. Stat. 709.02 covers houses with one to four units. A completed report must reach the buyer within 10 days of acceptance, or the buyer can cancel in the next two business days and recover deposits. Section 709.02 also lets a seller rely on written findings from an engineer, surveyor, pest control operator or contractor for matching entries.

The transfer fee under Wis. Stat. 77.22 is 30 cents per $100 of value, paid by the grantor. At the $417,400 median home value in Muskego, that fee is $1,252.20 (4,174 hundreds at 30 cents).

How do you record a deed with the Waukesha County Register of Deeds?

Muskego lies in Waukesha County. The Recording page lists $30 for standard documents such as deeds and mortgages. The office accepts check or money order made out to the Register of Deeds only, with no cash, credit or debit. If a transfer fee is due, include it with the payment.

Provide an email address or a self-addressed stamped envelope so the recorded document can come back. Email returns are immediate, and mailed returns take two to three weeks. The office is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays at 262-548-7585 and cannot give legal advice, so use a title company or attorney for the deed itself.

When are Muskego property taxes due?

The Wisconsin Department of Revenue's Guide for Property Owners explains that first-half payments are due January 31 and second-half payments July 31. Late first installments make the whole balance delinquent on February 1. Ask the City of Muskego treasurer for the current bill and any special charges before your closing, and let the closing agent divide the year's tax.

Assessments follow market value on January 1, and owners who disagree can use the Open Book and Board of Review process described in the guide. Ask the city assessor for this year's dates.

When is a cash sale the better fit in Muskego?

A cash buyer fits a Muskego seller who wants fewer steps: no showings, no buyer loan to approve, and no repair list negotiated after an inspection. A listing can bring a higher price from a buyer who finances, and you give up some speed.

  • Request the offer in writing with the closing date.

No. The office accepts check or money order made payable to the Register of Deeds for recording fees.

What is De Pere like, and how does the layout affect a home sale?

De Pere grew up around the first and last rapids on the lower Fox River. A French Jesuit mission was founded there in 1671, and the city traces its modern plat to 1836, when the De Pere Hydraulic Company laid out the town. The east and west banks were separate municipalities for decades. East De Pere became a city in 1883, and West De Pere (briefly named Nicolet) was folded into it in 1890, according to the city's Wikipedia entry.

That two-bank history still shapes the market. Large older homes line Broadway, Ridgeway Boulevard, Morris, Fulton, Franklin and nearby streets close to the river, and several of those blocks sit in National Register historic districts. St. Norbert College, founded in 1898, borders the river on the west side. Newer subdivisions sit away from the water, with Interstate 41 running along the west side of the city and Highways 32 and 57 entering from the south.

The city says two school districts serve De Pere, so check which one covers your address before you tell a buyer. Wikipedia also notes that the Lower Fox River below the De Pere dam went through a cleanup of PCB-contaminated sediment that was completed in 2020. If your house has been used as a short-term rental, ask the city's Development Services Department about its license status before you list. A buyer who plans to continue the use will ask.

Brown County has moved to tag-less recording. If you submit paper documents, you also submit a Swift Agreement, and you receive an email with a secure link that allows up to three printed copies for seven days.

How is Caledonia laid out, and why does it matter for a sale?

The village covers about 45 square miles along Lake Michigan, which makes it large by Wisconsin standards. It is made up of distinct communities: Franksville (the old Skunk Grove trading area), Husher, Tabor and others that began as trading posts, railroad stops and crossroads, according to the village's own history page. A buyer looking at a Franksville lot is comparing a different setting from someone looking near Douglas Avenue, and your listing or offer conversation should reflect that.

The village describes easy access to I-94, with Milwaukee 18 miles north and Chicago 73 miles south, plus two business parks (Caledonia and DeBack Farms) that supply local jobs. Commute length matters to buyers, and Census data puts the mean travel time to work for Caledonia residents at 25.8 minutes.

The land has deep roots. An Indian-French fur trader, Jacques Vieau, ran a trading post here around 1832, the Town of Caledonia was created by a territorial act on February 7, 1842, and Bohemian farmers settled in the Tabor area from 1849. How can you sell a house fast in Mequon, WI?

A buyer who takes the house as it is shortens the list of repairs, showings and negotiations before closing. You can also list with an agent or sell privately, and each route ends with a seller's condition report, a transfer return and a recorded deed.

The Census Bureau reports for Mequon a median owner-occupied home value of $501,600 and an 86.0% owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024. With values at that level, a repair credit or a price cut moves real money, so sellers here weigh an as-is sale against the cost and time of fixing the house.

What is Mequon, Wisconsin like?

Mequon is a city in Ozaukee County about 15 miles north of Milwaukee, on the western shore of Lake Michigan. It covers 48.77 square miles, and as of 2005 it was the third-largest city by land area in the state. Roughly half of the land is undeveloped or farmed, so lots here vary widely in size and in the services that reach them. The Village of Thiensville sits as an enclave in the middle of the city. The city borders Cedarburg and Grafton to the north, Germantown to the west, and Bayside, River Hills, Brown Deer and Milwaukee to the south. Much of the shoreline has mixed gravel and sand beaches, and the soil is clayey glacial till, which is worth knowing if you plan to dig a foundation or a pond.

The Town of Mequon incorporated as a city in 1957 under the state's Oak Creek Law, which was written to keep suburban towns from being annexed. Germans became the largest ethnic group in the 1840s. Growth followed I-43 in the 1960s, and the lakefront runs along clay bluffs that range from 80 to 140 feet high, cut by ravines where streams reach the lake.

Winter highs average about 27 degrees in January and July highs about 81 degrees. The Ozaukee Interurban Trail, a former passenger rail line, runs north to south through the city, and I-43 reaches it through exits 85, 87 and 89.
